solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl formed policy

parts.note: formed, as in made or shaped, gives MADE
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Someone or something shaped a policy, read as a news snippet.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeline is a female first name, so it fits the general word for a young woman.

clue.text: Greed is a bad habit overwhelming a king

indicators.note: overwhelming suggests one thing swamping and enclosing another, so a vice surrounds the king

parts.note: a vice is a bad habit
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: A moral observation that greed is a vice strong enough to overcome even a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greed is a bad habit' reads as one statement, but 'is' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is a direct synonym for greed, an excessive desire for wealth.

clue.text: Craft appearing in what is our home

indicators.note: appearing in puts the craft word inside the word for what

parts.note: eh? is a way of saying what? when you have not heard
craft as a skill is art

explanation.surface: A question of where a craft fits within our world.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet we all live on is our home world, a cryptic but fair description.

clue.text: One's hiding the onset of fresh uncertainties

indicators.note: hiding means the first word covers up and holds the letter taken from fresh

parts.note: One's is I'S, roman numeral one plus the apostrophe s

indicators.note: the onset of means the start, so only the first letter of fresh is used

explanation.surface: Someone concealing the start of new doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifs are conditions or doubts, as in 'no ifs or buts', so they are uncertainties.

clue.text: Regular boy at Grammar School providing services later

parts.note: even means regular or steady
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy attending a grammar school regularly, who will later be of service.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a grammar school is a selective state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, held later in the day than the morning ones.

clue.text: Run into horse, as donkeys do

indicators.note: into says the run letter goes inside the horse word

parts.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Bumping into a horse while making the noise a donkey makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys make a loud harsh cry, the verb for which is this word.

clue.text: Be served rum, eg, in this? Probably something else

definitions.text: Be served rum, eg, in this? Probably something else

indicators.note: served, as in dished up or turned out, signals the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of rum and eg

explanation.surface: You might be given rum in this vessel, but more likely another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: BE stays as it is, and 'served' rearranges RUM EG; the whole clue jokes that rum is rarely drunk from one: beer is the 'something else'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankard is meant for beer, the drink it is named after, rather than spirits such as rum.

clue.text: A thing I don't have, I regret to say!

parts.note: a lack is something you are without

explanation.surface: Someone sadly confessing to something they are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an archaic exclamation of sorrow, as in 'alas and alack'.

clue.text: Initially hostile atmosphere that grows on one

indicators.note: Initially means only the first letter of hostile is taken

parts.note: air means atmosphere

explanation.surface: A frosty mood that you gradually come to like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grows on one' suggests something you come to like; here it is literal growth on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is what literally grows on a person's head and body.

clue.text: Seek tall eccentric, very thin

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: An instruction to find an odd, lanky, skinny person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skeletal is so thin that their bones show.

clue.text: Bloke Colin has upset

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some man has unsettled Colin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas is a man's first name, so it is an example of a bloke, British slang for a man.

clue.text: Take some glen in, gradually finding old city

indicators.note: Take some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to absorb a valley slowly, ending up at a historic city.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'finding' in the definition; it is only a link word, since 'finding old city' cannot stand in for the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Leningrad was the Soviet-era name of St Petersburg, so it is a former name of a city.

clue.text: You'll see me holding one, karaoke just starting?

definitions.text: You'll see me holding one, karaoke just starting?

indicators.note: holding means the word me grips the other letters inside it

parts.note: I is the roman numeral for one

indicators.note: just starting means only the first letter of karaoke is wanted

explanation.surface: A singer about to begin karaoke saying you'll spot them gripping the equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a karaoke singer holds a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mike is a microphone, the thing a karaoke singer holds.

clue.text: Cardinal knew many on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside says the answer lies within the letters of knew many

explanation.surface: A cardinal who was acquainted with many insiders in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' could be a number or a colour; here it is a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: John Henry Newman was a famous Victorian cardinal, later canonised.

clue.text: Gruesome, when taxi goes into horse

indicators.note: goes into tells us the taxi word is placed inside the horse word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A horrible scene of a taxi crashing into a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means grim and horrifying, especially concerning death, so it matches gruesome.

clue.text: Head's briefly g-gone back home

indicators.note: back means the shortened word is read in reverse order
briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a stammered gone, giving the letters GGONE
in means at home

explanation.surface: A stammering report that someone's head has gone back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the E from GGONE to leave GGON, and 'back' turns it round to NOGG before IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Noggin is informal slang for a person's head.

clue.text: Not at all popular now, indeed

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
ay is an old word for yes, used to agree or affirm, like indeed

explanation.surface: A firm denial that something is fashionable these days.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic negative, meaning by no means.

clue.text: Countries, perhaps, united, behold, in ancient times

indicators.note: in places the behold word within the letters for ancient times

parts.note: BC, before Christ, marks ancient times
lo is an old word meaning behold

explanation.surface: An old-world image of nations united in ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of nations allied for a common purpose, such as the Eastern bloc.

clue.text: Praise a champion racing driver

parts.note: laud means praise

explanation.surface: A tribute to a winning motor racer.
explanation.definitionFit: Niki Lauda was an Austrian Formula One driver who won the world championship three times.

clue.text: Listening out after releasing one small bird

indicators.note: out suggests something is wrong or disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
releasing means letting go of one letter from the fodder before the rearrangement

parts.note: I is the roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone eavesdropping who then lets a little bird free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'releasing one' removes an I from LISTENING, and 'out' scrambles LSTENING.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a baby bird too young to leave the nest, so a small bird.

clue.text: Composer's Shakespearean king eclipsing Henry

indicators.note: eclipsing means covering, so the king word surrounds the Henry letter

parts.note: King Lear is a Shakespeare tragedy
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A composer's royal character outshining another king called Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry' looks like another Shakespearean king, but it gives only H.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of the operetta The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Fruit: happy to consume the third of four pounds!

indicators.note: to consume means the happy word swallows the other letters

parts.note: merry means happy

indicators.note: the third of means take the third letter of four

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for pounds in weight

explanation.surface: Someone delighted to eat a fruit costing a portion of four pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A mulberry is a dark berry from the mulberry tree.

clue.text: Hype is oddly lacking, I agree

indicators.note: oddly lacking means the odd-numbered letters are missing, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing that something has a curious absence of hype.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes is the word of assent, said when one agrees.

clue.text: Offer for sale? You've got to cough up!

definitions.meaning: to ... goods is to peddle them in the street
to clear the throat noisily, bringing up phlegm

explanation.surface: A street seller telling a customer they must pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cough up' suggests paying money, but here it is literal throat-clearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: peddling wares, and clearing phlegm from the throat.

clue.text: Lass finishes off black tea: not nice

indicators.note: finishes off points to the last letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A girl drinking the last of some unpleasant black tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate is a girl's name, an example of a lass, a northern British word for a girl.

clue.text: Empty desolate steamship, with ancient city in ruins

indicators.note: Empty means the inside of desolate is removed, keeping only its outer letters
in puts the ancient city inside the steamship letters

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad

explanation.surface: A deserted ship lying wrecked in an old ruined city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' looks like a noun at the end of the scene; it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck it completely, the same as the verb in the answer.
